reason: While the text clearly shows that the people are suffering—explicitly stated as 'וַיַּ֖רְא בְּסִבְלֹתָ֑ם' (he saw their burdens/afflictions)—there is no indication that this suffering is their own fault. The passage depicts Hebrews under Egyptian oppression, with Egyptians beating Hebrew laborers. The suffering is externally imposed through slavery and violent subjugation by their Egyptian masters, not caused by the people's own actions or culpability. The passage presents the Hebrews as victims of oppression, not as people suffering due to their own wrongdoing.
